title: Phase 6 never asserts the snapshot describes the same staker addresses Phase 0 checks: no `.address`/`.chainId` provenance probe, and `resolveAddress()` accepts 0x0
fingerprintNote: Carried VERBATIM from classified-findings.json; not recomputed by finding-manager.
description: `_loadSnapshotUsers` reads only `.stakers.<key>.users` from scripts/snapshots/depletion-stakers-latest.json. The snapshot file DOES record `.stakers.<key>.address` (verified: all three currently equal V1_STAKER_EYE/SCX/FLX exactly), but the script never cross-checks it against its own constants, never checks the file's `blockNumber` for staleness, and never checks the file exists at all before Phases 1-5 are queued. Upstream, scripts/snapshot-depletion-stakers.js:98-106 resolves those addresses by regex over server/deployments/mainnet-addresses.ts — the stale-trap pattern already recorded for this project, where that file has previously carried 0x000…0 'not deployed' placeholders for LIVE funded contracts; the regex `(0x[0-9a-fA-F]{40})` accepts a zero placeholder as a valid match. RECONCILIATION: this is the same missing-Phase-0-probe root cause as run-22 L-07 (b28492ce…) and should be collapsed into it by the deduplicator; the address-provenance and staleness dimensions are the increment L-07 did not cover.
impact: No assets are stolen, no user stake is lost, and NO partially-applied cutover occurs. The failure is an ATOMIC PRE-BROADCAST ABORT: forge runs `run()` as a single local EVM frame before dispatching anything, so a revert at :1550 unwinds Phases 1-5 in full - zero transactions signed, zero mined - and forge's non-zero exit halts the `&&` chain in package.json:288 so the patch and verify legs never run. What remains is a precondition-hygiene defect on a one-shot, hardware-signed mainnet cutover: Phase 6 never asserts that the snapshot targeted the same staker addresses Phase 0 asserts on. The snapshot file records `.stakers.<key>.address` and `.chainId`, but `_loadSnapshotUsers` (:1599-1601) reads only `.users`; `resolveAddress()` in scripts/snapshot-depletion-stakers.js:98-106 will accept a `0x000...0` placeholder as a valid 40-hex match. A mis-resolved snapshot is therefore caught LATE and only INCIDENTALLY - by the empty-user-list guard at :1550, which fires on the symptom (an empty list) rather than on the cause (a wrong address) - instead of by an explicit Phase 0 precondition that would name the actual problem. The operator cost is a late, mis-attributed abort and a re-run, not a broken protocol. For scale: the three NFTStakerDepletion instances hold 1 / 2 / 3 users respectively (UniboostStakerEYE / SCX / FLX). The figures 2 / 156 / 13 that appeared in the prior version of this record are STAKE UNITS from the migrate log, NOT user counts - see `factualCorrections`.
attackPath: 1. No attacker is required. The precondition is operational: `npm run promotion-ready:snapshot` is re-run before the broadcast (the runbook requires a fresh list).

2. scripts/snapshot-depletion-stakers.js:98-106 resolves the three staker addresses by regex `(0x[0-9a-fA-F]{40})` over server/deployments/mainnet-addresses.ts. The regex accepts a `0x000...0` 'not deployed' placeholder as a valid match, and this project has already produced exactly that state (project memory: mainnet-addresses stale trap).

3. The snapshot is written targeting a wrong, zero, or superseded staker address. Its `.stakers.<key>.address` records the address actually used - but nothing ever reads that field, and `.chainId` is never checked either.
4. Phase 0 asserts on the script's own V1_STAKER_EYE/SCX/FLX constants and passes. It never opens the snapshot file, so the mismatch is invisible at the point where it could be named.

5. UNPROVEN STEP - see `validatorFindings.causalInertness`. For the defect to surface at all, the mis-resolved address must yield an EMPTY (or stake-inconsistent) user list. This causal step was ASSERTED, never demonstrated: `_loadSnapshotUsers` reads only `.users`, so corrupting `.address` alone reverts NOTHING. A snapshot with a wrong `.address` but an intact `users` array migrates the correct users and completes green.
6. Where step 5 does hold, forge's LOCAL pass executes Phases 1-5 in-memory and then Phase 6 reverts at :1550 ('snapshot user list is empty but V1 still holds stake').

7. Outcome: the ENTIRE local frame unwinds. Nothing was broadcast, because forge had not begun dispatching. forge exits non-zero, the `&&` chain stops, and the operator re-runs after fixing the snapshot. The residual defect is diagnostic quality and the absence of an explicit precondition - NOT a partially-applied cutover.
likelihood: low-to-medium as a trigger, but the consequence is benign. It needs no attacker and no owner malice, only a mis-resolved snapshot address - a condition this project has produced before on these exact three contracts. It is bounded downward twice: the CURRENT snapshot file is correct (all three `.address` fields equal the script constants), and a wrong `.address` on its own is causally inert.
assumptions: (1) The snapshot is regenerated before the broadcast rather than the verified-good current file being reused. (2) resolveAddress picks up a zero placeholder or a superseded address from server/deployments/mainnet-addresses.ts.
externalRequirements: The off-chain state file server/deployments/mainnet-addresses.ts must be stale or carry a zero placeholder at snapshot time. This is external to the Solidity, and is the documented realized failure mode on this project — it is a stated external requirement, not a hand-wavy hypothetical.
evidence: Source :1599-1601 (`_loadSnapshotUsers` reads `.users` only); guard :1550; post-migrate guards :1553-1554; Phase 7 backstop :1697-1699. package.json:287 (the project's own statement of the local-pass-precedes-broadcast mechanism) and :288 (the `&&` chain). scripts/snapshot-depletion-stakers.js:98-106. Snapshot inspected at scripts/snapshots/depletion-stakers-latest.json: chainId 1, all three `.address` fields match the script constants, user counts 1 / 2 / 3. Adversarial validation: `forge script` without `--broadcast` - both broadcast-recorded actions rolled back, exit 1, nothing dispatched.
recommendation: Add a Phase 0 snapshot-provenance probe, before any mutation, requiring `.stakers.<key>.address == V1_STAKER_<X>` for all three stakers and `.chainId == 1`, and rejecting the zero address. Cost: three string comparisons on a file Phase 0 must open anyway. Separately, harden `resolveAddress()` at scripts/snapshot-depletion-stakers.js:98-106 to reject `0x000...0` explicitly rather than accepting it as a valid 40-hex match - that closes the realized upstream cause. The benefit is DIAGNOSTIC, not availability: the run already aborts safely and atomically, but it aborts on the symptom ('user list is empty') rather than the cause ('this snapshot is for a different address'). NOTE for the fix author: file-EXISTENCE probing and `.blockNumber` freshness belong to open ledger entry L-07 (b28492ce...) per SN-23-01 and should land in the same Phase 0 block.

poc.doesNotProveImpact: This PoC must NOT be presented as proving the finding's impact. It does not demonstrate a partially-applied cutover, because no such state exists in the real invocation.
whatItActuallySupports: (a) The :1550 guard exists, is fail-closed, and emits exactly `snapshot user list is empty but V1 still holds stake`.
(c) ONLY under a COUNTERFACTUAL model - where Phases 1-5 and Phase 6 are separate TOP-LEVEL transactions - does Phase 1-5 state survive the Phase 6 revert.
poc.harnessCaveat: The harness splits `run()` at the Phase 5 / Phase 6 boundary into two external entry points (its own header calls this 'a DEVIATION ... forced by the EVM'). That split has NO counterpart in the real invocation, where `run()` is a single local EVM frame. The counterfactual is the entire source of the harness's surviving state.
poc.provenance: AUDIT-AUTHORED and UNTRACKED in the upstream repo. Never present it as an upstream project test.
poc.retainedBecause: It is a correct and useful artifact for claims (a)-(c); it is re-scoped, not deleted.

evidenceCorrection.impactOnSeverity: SUPERSEDED 2026-08-03. The line-number corrections themselves remain exact and stand. But the sentence 'All corrected guards remain inside Phase 6 / Phase 7, which confirms the mid-sequence framing the Medium rests on' is RETRACTED: guard PLACEMENT inside run() is irrelevant, because the whole of run() executes as one local EVM frame before any dispatch. See `severityWalkedBack`.

severityWalkedBack.basis: PoC validation refuted the mid-sequence premise. forge executes `run()` as ONE local EVM frame first and dispatches only if that frame returns successfully; a later revert unwinds the entire frame. An independent probe (`forge script` without `--broadcast`) confirmed both broadcast-recorded actions were rolled back, forge exited 1, and nothing dispatched. `--skip-simulation` skips the per-tx pre-send check, NOT the local pass. The guard's inputs (`users.length` from `vm.readFile`, `preTotal` from local forked state) are fully deterministic in the local pass, so :1550 ALWAYS fires pre-broadcast. This is the ForgeLocalPassPrecedesBroadcast family already on this ledger from run-22; the Medium inverted the family's own semantics. The project's own package.json:287 states the mechanism verbatim.
severityWalkedBack.supersedes: The prior `justification` field's discriminator - 'L-07's impact is atomic pre-broadcast, which is why L-07 is a Low and F-06 is not' - is FALSE and is retained below only as `justificationRetracted`. Both are atomic pre-broadcast.
severityWalkedBack.severityNow: low - a missing explicit precondition on a one-shot script; the failure mode it guards against is caught, fail-closed, atomically, before any transaction is signed.

justificationRetracted: Upgraded to Medium, and the upgrade rests entirely on WHEN the guard fires, not on any new claim about what it catches. The finding is NOT that a bad migration slips through — it cannot; the code is fail-closed and that is stated plainly. The finding is that the only guard sits at :1550/:1553-1554, deep inside Phase 6, whereas its cost could be paid for by a single `require` in Phase 0 comparing the snapshot's own recorded `.address` fields against V1_STAKER_EYE/SCX/FLX. On a repeatable script this is a Low: you re-run it. On a one-shot, irreversible, hardware-signed mainnet cutover, converting an atomic pre-broadcast abort into a mid-sequence revert IS the impact — 'the function of the protocol or its availability could be impacted' is met squarely, with the assumption and external requirement both stated and both historically realized. This is precisely the discriminator the deduplicator used to refuse the collapse into L-07: L-07's own recorded impact is 'atomic, before a single transaction is broadcast', which is why L-07 is correctly a Low and why F-06 is not. Medium and no higher: no assets are at direct risk, nothing is stolen, and the fail-closed rails hold, so the High bar is not approached.
justification: LOW. The Medium rested entirely on WHEN the guard fires - 'converting an atomic pre-broadcast abort into a mid-sequence revert IS the impact'. That premise is empirically false (see `severityWalkedBack`): there is no mid-sequence state on this script, because forge's local pass precedes any dispatch and unwinds atomically. With the availability impact gone, what is left is a missing explicit precondition and a late, mis-attributed error message on a one-shot script - QA/Low: a spec/state-handling issue with no asset risk and no availability impact. Not suppressed, because the recommendation is cheap, the upstream `resolveAddress()` zero-address hole is real and historically realized, and it shares a Phase 0 fix site with open entry L-07.

refutation.claimRefuted: A mis-resolved snapshot yields a partially-applied, irreversible mainnet cutover because the guards sit inside Phase 6 after Phases 1-5 dispatched.
refutation.observation: forge runs `run()` as ONE local EVM frame and dispatches only if that frame returns successfully. A later revert unwinds the whole frame: both broadcast-recorded actions were rolled back, forge exited 1, nothing dispatched.
refutation.notes: `--skip-simulation` skips the per-tx pre-send check, NOT the local pass. The guard's inputs (`users.length` from `vm.readFile`, `preTotal` from local forked state) are deterministic in the local pass, so :1550 always fires pre-broadcast.
refutation.family: ForgeLocalPassPrecedesBroadcast - already on this ledger from run-22, and stated verbatim by the project's own package.json:287. This finding inverted the family's own semantics.

causalInertness.finding: The address mismatch is causally inert on its own.
causalInertness.detail: `_loadSnapshotUsers` (:1599-1601) reads only `.users` and never `.address`. A probe that corrupted `.address` while leaving `users` intact reverted NOTHING - the run completed. Only an EMPTY user list fires :1550, and the PoC set that by FIXTURE CONSTRUCTION.
causalInertness.consequence: The causal step 'mis-resolved address => empty/wrong user list' was ASSERTED, never demonstrated. This materially weakens the finding and is recorded here rather than omitted (Law 1: visible, not silent).
causalInertness.residualValidity: The recommendation still stands on its own terms - an explicit `.address`/`.chainId` provenance assertion plus a zero-address reject in `resolveAddress()` is cheap and closes a historically realized upstream hole - but the finding may NOT be graded on a demonstrated causal chain, because none was demonstrated.

factualCorrections.wrong: The prior `impact` described the three stakers as covering '2 / 156 / 13 users'.
factualCorrections.correct: Those are STAKE UNITS from the migrate log. The actual snapshot user counts are 1 / 2 / 3 (UniboostStakerEYE 1, UniboostStakerSCX 2, UniboostStakerFLX 3), verified directly from scripts/snapshots/depletion-stakers-latest.json.
factualCorrections.notFixedIn: Upstream pipeline stage artifacts retain the erroneous phrasing as the historical record of what each stage emitted and were deliberately NOT rewritten: script-audits/promotion-ready-broadcast/classified-findings.json:64 (assetImpact) and the corresponding candidate/sanitized entries. They are SUPERSEDED by this record and must not be quoted downstream. Note that intent.md:19 ('conservation OK at 2 / 156 / 13 units') and side-effects.json:66 ('totalStaked 2/156/13') are CORRECT - they say units, not users.

relationToRun22L07.falseDiscriminatorRetracted: The dedup discriminator that originally kept them separate - 'L-07 is atomic pre-broadcast, F-06 is mid-sequence' - is FALSE. BOTH are atomic pre-broadcast. This false basis is retracted and must not stand anywhere.
relationToRun22L07.correctedBasisForSeparation: Different ROOT CAUSE and different FIX. L-07 is FILE ABSENCE / STALENESS with no Phase 0 probe - the file is missing or old. This entry is CONTENT PROVENANCE - the file may exist and be perfectly fresh yet describe the WRONG ADDRESSES. Fixing L-07 (probe that the file exists and `.blockNumber` is fresh) does not fix this entry, and vice versa.
relationToRun22L07.fix: Assert `.stakers.<key>.address == V1_STAKER_<X>` for all three stakers and `.chainId == 1`, and reject the zero address in `resolveAddress()` (scripts/snapshot-depletion-stakers.js:98-106).
relationToRun22L07.supersedes: SN-23-01's stated rationale. Both entries cross-reference each other; both fixes belong in the same Phase 0 block so the operator implements one probe, not two.
